# Registry Stack

> Registry Stack is open-source infrastructure that helps government registries return signed minimum-disclosure answers or protected, selected data while source records stay with the authority that holds them. Evidence Gateway and Protected Registry APIs are the two product paths; Evidence and Registry Relay are their independent runtimes. Registry Mint and Registry Manifest provide supporting token and metadata capabilities. Aubex Consulting LLC provides pilot delivery and commercial support.

## Pages

- [Home](https://registrystack.org/): How Registry Stack helps a registry owner provide signed answers or selected data.
- [Evidence Gateway](https://registrystack.org/solutions/evidence-gateway/): Return one signed, minimum-disclosure assertion for a predefined question.
- [Protected Registry APIs](https://registrystack.org/solutions/protected-registry-apis/): Provide read-only access to agreed registry fields without distributing the source.
- [Use cases](https://registrystack.org/use-cases/): Worked public-service scenarios and how to choose between a signed answer and selected data.
- [How it fits](https://registrystack.org/how-it-fits/): Registry Stack is deployed next to the source registry and before any exchange layer; the page also covers identity systems, catalogs, and standards.
- [Pilot and support](https://registrystack.org/pilot/): What is open source, what paid help covers, and how to start with one registry.
- [Security](https://registrystack.org/security/): The security model: what it protects, what a deployment can reach, and the threat model in and out of scope.
- [FAQ](https://registrystack.org/faq/): Short answers to the questions program teams, security reviewers, and engineers ask first.

## Related sites

- [Documentation](https://docs.registrystack.org/): Technical reference and specifications for Evidence, Registry Relay, Registry Mint, and Registry Manifest.
- [Live demo](https://lab.registrystack.org/): A hosted lab running the full stack on synthetic data only.
